validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solidly real, extensively documented across 3 decades of primary sources. UTOS ("U-T Offshore System") is a 42-inch, ~29-30 mile natural gas pipeline built in 1978 running from the Gulf of Mexico (West Cameron Block 167) to Johnson's Bayou, Cameron Parish, Louisiana -- confirmed by a 2011 PHMSA Part 192.3 interpretation letter (then-operator Enbridge Offshore Pipelines (UTOS) L.L.C.), a Feb 2026 PHMSA Corrective Action Order (CPF 4-2026-028-CAO) issued to current operator Delfin Offshore Pipeline LLC after a real 2026 rupture/explosion on this exact line, Oil & Gas Journal, naturalgasworld.com, and offshore-technology.com. DUPLICATE: NOT a duplicate of any other row in the 41-row roster -- P0200 HIOS is a physically distinct, upstream, interconnecting system (the 2011 PHMSA letter and the 2026 CAO both independently describe HIOS and UTOS as two separate pipelines joined at WC-167); P6584 ANR Offshore Grand Chenier is a third, separate 30-inch line (see cross_row_leads). ATTRIBUTION: current owner Delfin LNG LLC (100%, per delfinmidstream.com) and current operator Delfin Offshore Pipeline LLC (per the 2026 PHMSA CAO, addressed to CEO Dudley Poston) both check out -- Delfin acquired the pipeline from Enbridge in 2014 (3 independent sources: lnglawblog.com, offshore-technology.com, naturalgasworld.com all state the 2014 Enbridge->Delfin sale). CAVEAT: this row's classification (see companion 'classification' concern) and two date fields (StopYear, Proposal/Construction) needed correction -- see the concern + fills below.

validity.recommendation: change PipelineType from 'both transmission and gathering' to 'transmission' -- the current value is neither valid controlled vocabulary nor supported by the row's own cited source
validity.researcher_notes: TWO separate problems with the recorded PipelineType='both transmission and gathering': (1) it is not valid controlled vocabulary -- docs/reference/controlled_vocab.md lists only 'transmission', 'gathering', 'distribution' for PipelineType; 'both transmission and gathering' does not appear as an option (unlike, e.g., P0200 HIOS in this same batch, whose 'both transmission and gathering' value IS directly supported by its own cited PHMSA letter -- see that row's shard). (2) It is directly contradicted by the very document already cited in this row's own PipelineType [ref] cell: the March 8, 2011 PHMSA Part 192.3 interpretation letter to Enbridge Offshore Pipelines (UTOS) L.L.C. states verbatim: 'We agree with [FERC] that certain portions of the HIOS are used for the gathering of gas, but that the pipeline segment that interconnects with the UTOS is a transmission line... For that reason, we further conclude that the UTOS cannot be a gathering line under 49 CFR Sec. 192.3.' PHMSA's own regulatory determination is that UTOS is transmission only -- gathering classification applies to portions of the upstream HIOS system (P0200), not to UTOS itself. Recommend PipelineType='transmission'. Single-source (this letter is the only document found that directly addresses UTOS's regulatory classification), so tier is medium per this project's single-regulator-filing convention, but it is dispositive: a federal regulator's own determination, already cited by the sheet, that the sheet's classification is simply wrong.

Two 2019/2020-era trade-press sources (naturalgasworld.com's LNG Condensed project spotlight, and offshore-technology.com's project page) DO independently state 'abandoned in 2011 due to decrease in flow volumes' -- matching the sheet. However, PHMSA's own Feb 6, 2026 Corrective Action Order (CPF 4-2026-028-CAO, issued directly to operator Delfin Offshore Pipeline LLC after a real Feb 3, 2026 rupture on this exact pipeline during pigging operations) states with operational specificity: 'In 2012, a prior operator purged, isolated, and filled the Delfin Offshore Gas Pipeline with nitrogen. The pipeline has remained out of service since that time.' NaturalGasIntel's Feb 12, 2026 reporting on the same CAO independently states 'The pipeline, which has been out of service since 2012...' I am recommending 2012 (contradicting the two older press pieces) because: (a) it is a primary federal regulatory investigative finding, ranking above trade press per source_roster.md; (b) it carries specific operational detail (nitrogen purge/isolation procedure) rather than a generic 'abandoned' description; (c) it is the most recent and most directly-informed source (issued in direct response to inspecting this pipeline). This is a close call and a genuinely material 1-year discrepancy -- flagging explicitly rather than silently overriding.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Much more current evidence than LastUpdated (2024-07-16) found and it CONFIRMS idle, though the story is more dramatic than the sheet reflects. Timeline reconstructed from the PHMSA CAO and press: the pipeline had been shut-in and nitrogen-filled since 2012 (see the Stop fill/concern re: 2011-vs-2012). Delfin, working toward reactivating it as feedgas infrastructure for its Delfin FLNG deepwater export project (which reached a reported ~$5B FID around June 2026 per press coverage not independently re-verified in this pass), was running a cleaning pig with an in-line inspection tool through the line on Feb 3, 2026 when the pig struck a closed valve, gas was re-injected/ignited, and the line RUPTURED near Mae's Beach/Johnson Bayou -- a fire 50-80 ft wide burned for hours, ~56 MMcf of gas was released, one worker was injured (later suing Delfin, Genesis and others -- Kherkher Garcia LLP suit, Harris County), and Johnson Bayou High School (6 mi away) briefly sheltered in place. PHMSA issued Corrective Action Order CPF 4-2026-028-CAO on Feb 6, 2026 (case status OPEN per primis.phmsa.dot.gov), confirming as of that date: 'The pipeline is currently shut-in and not operating' and capping any eventual restart at 20% of MAOP pending a third-party investigation, remedial work plan, and hydrostatic testing (first progress report due April 1, 2026; case remains open as of this Sept 2026 review with no restart confirmed in any source found). NET: the pipeline never actually returned to service during this incident -- it ruptured WHILE being prepared for reactivation, and remains shut-in. 'idle' is therefore still the correct Status, now with dramatically fresher and more detailed evidence than the sheet had. Recommend also watching for a status change to 'construction' or 'operating' once/if PHMSA authorizes restart -- no evidence of that as of the most recent sources found (Feb 2026).

This directly names P6584 (ANR Offshore Grand Chenier, the batch's other idle row) and asserts CURRENT ownership by Delfin Midstream via subsidiary Avocet LNG -- worth checking against P6584's recorded owner (presumed ANR/TC Energy legacy ownership) since this suggests a same-pattern acquisition to UTOS's 2014 Enbridge->Delfin sale. Corroborated on diameter/capacity by ogj.com: 'Grand Chenier (30-in. OD, 700 MMcfd)'.
